reviews.specification:
Current-conversation Codex handoff: implement assay-woven-supports@1, independently learnable, with code reuse from food-assay recorded separately from functional equivalence. Public strict schema: {mode: enum[test-beam,test-vine,assemble,calibrate,resume], target:string, controls:string[], project:string, x:number, y:number}; all fields required, unused strings empty and controls empty. target and controls use shared owned-item resolution; project resolves an actor-owned persistent work record; x/y are explicit placement coordinates. Resolve and retain exact identities, never silently substitute inputs. Prerequisites: individual mastery of this interface; calibration and subsequent measurements additionally require food-assay mastery. No bark dependency.
Physical precursor: add branch bending, vine tension/knot-slip, woven-aperture and sample-retention tests using actual mass, dimensions, moisture and applied loads. Define versioned material laws for branch and vine, including conservative density, tensile/bending limits, wet weakening and creep; persist intrinsic physical parameters when first instantiated and apply the same laws to all interactions, without assigning successful suitability flags. Record these as modeled material parameters, not prior observations. Measure actual specimen dimensions and failures. test-beam and test-vine each take two performed rounds at 0.5 energy/round; allocate 0.1 unit of the selected material, retained afterward as tested material or fragments with exact mass/provenance. The retained owned hardness>=8 stone is a loading/working tool, not consumed. Test-vine includes wet and dry loading; any water must come from an actual reachable water source with finite withdrawn quantity and physical wetting, otherwise pause with a missing-input report. No free water. Tests report safe working load, deflection, creep and uncertainty; unknown or failed tests prohibit assembly approval rather than implying suitability.
Assembly allocates 1 branch and 3 vine units plus a retained hard stone and a distinct 1-unit stone subdivision source. Assign 1 vine to suspension, 1 to two woven baskets and 1 to a drying mesh. Material allocations become individually tracked components; subdivision conserves the second stone as five comparison pieces. Require a personally tested beam and vine batch whose measured safe loads exceed the computed loaded assembly forces by a factor of two. Twelve paid assembly rounds at 0.5 energy each construct a supported beam balance, two baskets and separate drying mesh; two further rounds at 0.5 energy subdivide the comparison stone. Fabrication cuts, ties and weaving must operate on represented components, conserve waste and record actual aperture, mass and geometry. No sheet material or hollow wooden pan is implied.
Placement requires clear supported ground, reachable within shared interaction distance 0.65: balance footprint 0.8 by 0.4, height 0.6; mesh footprint 0.4 by 0.4. Validate world bounds, shared collision geometry, hand access and swing clearance before committing placement. These are apparatuses, not rooms, shelter or comfort facilities. Calibration takes three rounds at 0.5 energy each, with actual tare, arm-length and repeated comparison readings; fail or report measured uncertainty if friction, unequal arms or creep prevents useful comparisons. Store working-load limits and calibration history.
Extend food-assay apparatus validation to accept this calibrated balance and mesh through a shared apparatus contract, retaining its existing paid reading, stability, wear and drying rules. Accept only intact samples experimentally shown to remain retained above the measured apertures; exclude liquids, powder and crumbling samples. Movement, shrinkage, fragments escaping, moisture transfer from the support and apparatus drift must update actual state and invalidate affected estimates. Escaped material becomes a real ground fragment, not vanished food. Food units, nutrients, toxins, water and processing lineage follow actual retained material; never infer safety or composition from residue. If basket tare changes, require a new actual tare measurement.
Persist component ownership, original allocations, spent energy, completed stages, exact remaining work, calibration and placement. Missing tools, energy, water or safe conditions pause without charges; global pauses preserve state. Action change, movement out of reach or death cancels active work exactly once. Consumed components remain in the partial apparatus; unconsumed surviving escrow returns once to its owner, or to the ground at death. Explicit resume locks that same partial apparatus and executes only its remaining paid stages after revalidation. Destruction produces conserved salvage, never full input refunds. Completion requires every stage and successful calibration; proposed products are not existing inventory. Maintain existing global budgets and knowledge/project limits. Migration adds apparatus variants and event subscriptions without altering existing bark apparatuses, food records or historical evidence; implementation and review advance no simulation time.
